summary: In a valid postfix sum, changing any operand token changes the result, so every operand—and therefore a linear fraction of all tokens—must be inspected. The stack evaluator matches this Omega(n) bound.

optimality.argument: Consider a valid left-associated postfix sum of m operands, represented by 2m - 1 tokens. Each operand can independently change from 1 to 2 while preserving validity and changing the final result. A correct evaluator must inspect all m operands in the worst case, which is Omega(n) token work. The current scan performs constant stack and arithmetic work per token, giving O(n) time.

replacement_checks.evidence: Every operand in a valid long postfix sum contributes to the answer, so skipping one cannot distinguish two expressions with different results.
Each token is read once and causes either one push or two pops, one arithmetic operation, and one push.

The source-fidelity-verified examples cover all four operators, nesting, negative operands, and truncating division; black-box real-test execution verifies every existing ordinary check without inspecting its definition.
